realistic.label: realistic
realistic.scene: Images 1 to {views} are frames of one location in a 2.5D game, all seen from the same fixed camera angle while the camera travels over it; Image {look_image} is a style reference only. Build one large, complete overview picture of the whole area these frames cover, from the same camera angle, perspective and scale: every place, building, structure, path, water, terrain feature and fixed prop exactly where the frames show it relative to the others, joined into one continuous place, with nothing invented between them beyond a natural continuation of the ground. Convert everything into realistic materials while keeping the style unchanged, taking the materials, lighting, colour grading, brightness and texture detail from Image {look_image} and nothing else (none of its objects, layout, UI or text). Leave out characters, animals, moving vehicles, carried items, UI, HUD, numbers, icons, buttons and all text: this is the empty location. Realistic materials of what is there (the list only describes materials, do not add anything because of it): {materials}. {look} {ground} Clean and sharp, no heavy noise and no broken or fragmented artifacts. {extra}
realistic.subject: Image 1 is a close crop of {what} from a 2.5D game video ({description}); Image 2 is the whole frame it comes from; Image 3 is the same video's location already converted into realistic materials. Make a turnaround reference sheet of {what} only: three complete views side by side (front, side and back), the same size, on a plain light grey background, evenly lit, nothing cropped. Keep its shape, proportions, colours, markings, clothing, equipment and number of parts exactly as in Image 1; only convert its materials into realistic real-world materials with the style unchanged, at the realism, lighting quality and texture detail of Image 3. No text, labels, captions or UI. {look}
realistic.video: Edit the video: replace the materials of the input video frame for frame, turning every game-rendered cartoon material into a realistic real-world material while keeping the style unchanged; the output is the same video, only with realistic materials. At every moment keep exactly the input video's high 2.5D camera position, angle, zoom and framing: the camera moves and cuts only where the input does, never a cut, a close-up, a zoom-in or a camera move of your own. Keep every character's action, the position, size, shape and count of every object and the timing exactly as in the input video; do not add, remove or move anything, and nothing appears before it appears in the input video. {refs} Realistic materials of what is on screen (the list only describes materials, do not add anything because of it): {materials}. {look} {ground} Keep the on-screen UI numbers, text, icons and buttons exactly as they are, crisp and legible. {remove}Do not add any new text or captions. No heavy noise, no broken or fragmented artifacts and no flicker; materials stay the same from frame to frame. {extra}

references.previous: Image {n} is the restyled frame where this clip begins, taken from the end of the previous part of this same video: the first frame of the output must look exactly like it (every object's materials, textures, colours, brightness, lighting and drawing, the ground included), and the whole clip keeps exactly that look, so the two parts join without any visible change.
references.scene: {images}: the whole location of this video already converted into realistic materials, seen from the same camera angle. Wherever the camera is, every place it shows must look exactly as there (ground, water, buildings, props, materials, textures, lighting, colour grading, brightness and level of realism); never fall back to the game's cartoon look.
references.subject: Image {n} is a three-view sheet (front, side, back) of {what}, already converted: whenever it is on screen, give it exactly the look of the sheet, at the size and place it has in the input video (the sheet shows it large only to show its look).
references.closing: The reference images are for look only: composition, camera, motion, timing and content come from the input video; do not add anything from them that the input video does not show.
references.motion: Image {n} is a motion reference only, not a look: three moments of the input video, {step} s apart from left to right, showing how the {what} move; in the result they move exactly the same way and at the same speed, advancing in every frame.
references.closing_motion: The other reference images are for look only: composition, camera, timing and content come from the input video; do not add anything from them that the input video does not show.

realistic.default_materials: realistic ground, water, ice and snow, wood, stone, metal, plants, cloth and character clothing
realistic.look: Overall look: real-world surface textures that stand out clearly (wood grain, bark, packed snow, ice, stone, rope fibres, fabric weave, fish scales), real light with natural shadows and contact shadows, crisp fine detail, clean; never pastel, glossy or cartoonish.
realistic.ground: The ground matters most for realism: every ground surface (soil, packed and loose snow, ice, gravel, planks) has a complex, deep and finely detailed texture with uneven relief, grain, small stones, cracks, drifts and trodden marks, crisp into the distance; never a smooth, flat or uniform fill.

remove: Remove these on-screen elements: {items}. Fill each area naturally with the surrounding scene and leave no trace; remove only these and keep every other text, number, sign and UI element unchanged.
